prompt.alinti: This might be the most powerful GitHub repo you can give Claude, and Microsoft open-sourced it.
It gives Claude a sleep cycle. Overnight, it practices the tasks you keep repeating and drafts better instructions, keeping only the changes that test better.
I tell my Claude the same rules every morning. It's like we've never met.
This repo writes it down for you.
It's called SkillOpt from Microsoft Research, and it has over 18,000 stars on GitHub.
Here's one night. It reads your past Claude code sessions, finds the tasks you keep repeating, and practices them again while you're away.
Then it drafts small rule edits for Claude's memory and skills.
Before it keeps an edit, it tests it on tasks it held back on purpose.
Score goes up, the edit is kept. No better, it's thrown out.
And nothing goes live until you type adopt with a backup of the old file.
Okay, how do I get it?

Three steps. One, clone the repo from GitHub. Two, in Claude code, add the plugin from the repo's plugins folder and install SkillOptSleep. Three, type slash SkillOptSleep dry run to preview what it would learn.
Then run, then adopt what you like.
Microsoft's own test with Claude Haiku took a deliberately weak skill from zero to perfect in one night.
The default mode is a free practice run with no AI calls, so switch the back end to Claude for real learning, which uses your own Claude usage.
And real mode sends snippets of your sessions to the model, so skip it on sensitive projects.
The three steps are on DripTheCup.com.
Send this to someone whose Claude keeps forgetting the rules.
